chunks.title: Credit memos in minutes · Overview
chunks.text: Credit memos in minutes, every figure cited. A multi-agent credit-risk and KYB product for financial institutions. Specialist agents research a company and write a cited credit memo; a second model checks every section, and high-risk calls wait for an analyst. Eight specialist agents read statements, filings and the web, then write a credit memo that a judge model checks. Organisation: TrustPlus AI. Year: 2025–26. Status: Employer. Theme: Multi-agent systems. Stack: LangGraph, LangChain, FastAPI, React, FAISS, Azure Service Bus, LangFuse.

chunks.title: Credit memos in minutes · My role
chunks.text: Designed and built most of the product across the stack, from requirements and customer proofs of concept to production, and was on call for it. The problem: Analysts spent most of a day assembling a credit memo from financial statements, filings and web research, then checking it by hand. The answer had to be faster without becoming less trustworthy.

chunks.title: Credit memos in minutes · How it works
chunks.text: Ingest: Statements, filings and web results enter an event-driven pipeline. Research: 8 specialist agents in LangGraph, each owning part of the memo. Retrieve: Hybrid search with rank fusion and reranking over FAISS. Check: A judge model checks each section against its sources. Approve: High-risk calls wait for an analyst; a chat edits the finished memo.

chunks.title: Credit memos in minutes · What I built
chunks.text: 8 specialist research agents orchestrated in LangGraph, with tool calling. Hybrid retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion and reranking over FAISS. A judge model, different from the writer, checks each section against its sources. Evaluation before release: golden test sets re-run on prompt and model changes, RAGAS for retrieval, LangFuse evaluations. Event-driven backend on Azure Service Bus with a LangChain multi-provider LLM layer and an Amazon Bedrock fallback.

chunks.title: Credit memos in minutes · Key decisions
chunks.text: Moved vector search from MongoDB to in-memory FAISS when parallel load hit I/O limits and a bigger tier cost too much. Separate judge and writer models, so a model never grades its own work. Per-step timing and error fields in the run state, so failures are visible to users and to on-call. Human approval only where the risk is high, so analysts review decisions, not typing.

chunks.title: Credit memos in minutes · Results
chunks.text: 5–60 min per memo, down from 6–24 hours. ~85% faster retrieval (700–1,400 ms to 100–250 ms). ~4 → ~20 releases a month after the move to Claude Code.

chunks.title: A role-fit agent · Overview
chunks.text: A role-fit agent, running on this site. The multi-agent system built into this portfolio. A visitor pastes a job description; an orchestrator, up to six parallel retrievers, a verifier and a writer return a cited fit report with the gaps listed, then answer follow-up questions in my voice. The verifier can send weak evidence back for a second search. No login, a hard monthly spend cap, and the whole run streams to the page as a live graph. Paste a job description and my agents check it against my published work. Every claim is an exact quote, and you watch the agent graph run live. Organisation: Personal. Year: 2026. Status: Open source. Theme: Multi-agent systems. Stack: Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, OpenAI Responses API, Server-sent events, BM25, TypeScript, React.

chunks.title: A role-fit agent · My role
chunks.text: Solo. I designed it and built it with Claude Code. The problem: A chatbot that answers questions about me proves very little. I wanted the site itself to run a real multi-agent system that a stranger can try without signing in, that cannot invent experience I do not have, and that cannot run up a bill.

chunks.title: A role-fit agent · How it works
chunks.text: Gate: Refuses anything that is not a job description. Orchestrate: Picks up to six requirements and the search terms for each. Retrieve: Six agents search in parallel and must quote exactly. Verify: A verifier checks every citation and can lower a verdict. Loop: Weak evidence goes back to the orchestrator for one more search. Write: A summary streams, then follow-up questions open.

chunks.title: A role-fit agent · What I built
chunks.text: An agent loop on a Cloudflare Worker: gate, orchestrator, up to six parallel retrievers, verifier, writer. When the verifier rejects evidence, the orchestrator chooses new search terms and up to three requirements go round once more. Code bounds the loop: two rounds and at most 15 model calls a run, each with a strict JSON schema and an output cap. A verdict can only be raised by new evidence that passes the same checks; the verifier itself can only lower one. Retrieval is BM25 over excerpts built from this site's case studies and my CV. Search runs in code; a model only judges what search found. Every quote must be an exact substring of the excerpt it cites, checked in code before it is shown. A claim with no surviving quote becomes a gap. Typed server-sent events stream each step with elapsed time, tokens and estimated cost. The page draws them as a live graph: nodes light up as they work, the loop back is drawn when it is taken, and clicking a node shows what it was asked and what it returned. Cached and recorded runs replay at the pace they really ran. A Durable Object ledger reserves the worst-case cost before every call and settles the real one afterwards, so the monthly cap is a hard limit and not an alert. No login: a signed anonymous token and a salted IP hash, a Turnstile check, 5 runs and 10 questions a day, and a 10-second gap between runs. Follow-up questions run their own short loop: memory, search, answer, verify, with one more search allowed. Memory is compacted, not cut: the last two turns stay word for word and older ones are folded into a running summary, kept on the server so the visitor cannot rewrite it.

chunks.title: A role-fit agent · Key decisions
chunks.text: A bounded loop over a free-roaming agent: the orchestrator decides what to retry, code decides how often, so the cost per run has a ceiling and every path can be tested with a scripted model. Keyword search over embeddings: a few hundred excerpts do not need a vector store, and every hit can be explained. Server-sent events over WebSockets: the stream only flows one way, and it needs no connection state. Guardrails in code, not in prompts: text that addresses the model is refused before any call, and the agent's prose is screened for links, leaked instructions and commitments made on my behalf. A small, cheap model with the harness doing the hard part: the model picks quotes, the code decides what is true enough to show.

chunks.title: A role-fit agent · Results
chunks.text: 15 model calls at most per run. $10 hard monthly spend cap. 78 automated tests.
